clue.text: Checked sappers under stress

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers, are abbreviated RE
someone under stress is strained

explanation.surface: Army engineers kept in line while working under heavy pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps whose soldiers are called sappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked in the sense of held back or kept under control is a synonym of restrained.

clue.text: Vestment in which the Archbishop of York turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Archbishop of York signs himself Ebor, from Eboracum, the Latin name of York

explanation.surface: Asking which ceremonial garment a senior churchman arrived in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses EBOR, the Archbishop of York's Latin signature, giving the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial garment, and a robe is a long flowing garment of that kind.

clue.text: Such a shoe makes him lose standing

definitions.text: Such a shoe makes him lose standing

parts.words: Such a shoe makes him lose standing
parts.note: a soft indoor shoe whose name suggests it would make the wearer lose his footing and fall over

explanation.surface: A type of footwear that topples a man, or costs him his social status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose standing' reads like losing reputation, but literally it means falling down, which is what this shoe's name suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft indoor shoe whose name also describes something that makes a person lose their footing.

clue.text: Anglers hope fish will fall into the net

explanation.surface: Fishermen waiting for a catch to be landed.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers want a fish to come up and take what they offer; figuratively the phrase means reacting to a provocation, being caught out like a trapped creature.

clue.text: Unseemly declaration of self-righteousness

explanation.surface: A prig's smug statement of virtue is itself in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PROPER, the answer is what a self-righteous person declares.
explanation.definitionFit: Unseemly behaviour is indecorous or wrong; read as two words, the answer is a boast of one's own propriety.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher takes note of top class

parts.note: in the Bible the priest Eli brought up and taught the boy Samuel
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A biblical tutor jotting down a remark about the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link: ELI is followed by TE.
explanation.definitionFit: The best or most select group in a society is the top class, its cream.

clue.text: Ray needs support

explanation.surface: A shaft of light needs something to hold it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of light is a shaft or beam; a beam is also a horizontal timber that supports a structure.

clue.text: Increase in general disorder

indicators.note: disorder tells us the letters of the preceding word are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A general state of chaos is growing.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase something in size is to make it bigger, to magnify it.

clue.text: Mum, is anyone making the dressing?

parts.note: mum and ma both mean mother

indicators.note: making signals that the following words are worked into something new, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Mother asking whether anybody is preparing the salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' looks like part of the question about cooking, but it signals that IS ANYONE is reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a thick egg-and-oil sauce used to dress salads.

clue.text: His musical works are sheer delight

explanation.surface: Someone's compositions are a pure joy to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Bliss was an English composer and Master of the Queen's Music.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was the English composer of those works; the word also means perfect happiness or joy.

clue.text: Novelist who sounded like a churchman

indicators.note: sounded tells us the word is pronounced the same as the writer's name

parts.note: behaving like a clergyman is being priestly

explanation.surface: A writer whose voice was as solemn as a clergyman's.
explanation.walkthrough: J. B. Priestley was the English author of novels such as The Good Companions; his surname is pronounced like the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: J. B. Priestley was an English writer of novels and plays such as An Inspector Calls.

clue.text: Practise selective avicide? Good heavens!

explanation.surface: Throwing rocks at only certain birds draws a shocked exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Avicide is the killing of birds; 'Stone the crows!' is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, pelting particular black birds with rocks; as an idiom it is an old British cry of astonishment.

clue.text: Interferes and starts a row

explanation.surface: Someone meddles and picks a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing a boat: a rower dips a paddle into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for meddling or giving unwanted advice; literally a rower lowers the paddle into the water to begin rowing.

clue.text: Made a summary despite being preoccupied

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a précis while their mind was elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract a document is to summarise it; someone abstracted is lost in thought and inattentive.

clue.text: Ban articles made of cloth

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article again

explanation.surface: Prohibiting items made of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives three pieces, A, THE and A, the English articles; 'made of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric with a broken rib weave, used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Enrage various classes

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of the preceding word in a different order

explanation.surface: Infuriating assorted groups of people.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, genera are categories ranking above species, so classes or kinds.

clue.text: Socialist rebukes distinguished philosopher

parts.note: to rate someone is an old word for scolding them

explanation.surface: A left-winger tells off an eminent thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' here is the old verb meaning to scold, not charges.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Athenian thinker who taught Plato is among the most famous of philosophers.

clue.text: A really good sort of hat

explanation.surface: Praise for a style of headgear that is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang calls a thoroughly decent person a topper; it is also a top hat.

clue.text: Mean, in the past, to unknown model

parts.note: par is the average or normal level
ago means at a time before now
in maths n stands for an unknown number

explanation.surface: Someone used to be cruel to a nameless fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like unkind but is the noun average, PAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to be copied, an ideal pattern.

clue.text: Neat workers intimidate masses of people

parts.note: to cow someone is to frighten them into submission
herds are crowds, large masses of people

explanation.surface: Tidy employees bully the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is the old word for cattle, not tidy; neat workers are those who tend cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for cattle, and these labourers look after cattle.

clue.text: After inactivity I have become uneasy

parts.note: rest is a period of inactivity
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone has grown restless after a spell of idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means fidgety and unable to stay calm, so restless or uneasy.

clue.text: Caesar's daring reforms displayed arrogance

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar's bold political changes showed his haughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of Caesar's is part of the anagram fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on airs and graces is to behave haughtily and affectedly, showing a superior manner.

clue.text: Cheat pocketed a pound — or double

indicators.note: pocketed means one piece has the other tucked inside it

parts.note: to dupe is to trick or cheat
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A swindler took a pound coin, or perhaps two.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, duple time has two beats to the bar, so twofold or double.

clue.text: Criminal needs talent

explanation.surface: An offender needs a natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for crooked or dishonest; a bent is also a natural aptitude or flair.

clue.text: Jam, pantihose and jumper brought back

parts.note: pantihose are tights

indicators.note: brought back means the word is reversed

parts.note: a jumper, a British word for a sweater, is a top

explanation.surface: A list of clothes, tights and a sweater, returned to a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a pullover sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a jam means being in a difficult situation or predicament.

clue.text: Appeal for donations to build an arch

parts.note: O is an exclamation used to address someone in an appeal
give is the plea made when asking for donations

explanation.surface: A fundraising campaign to pay for building an arch.
explanation.walkthrough: The appeal reads as 'O, give!'; 'to build' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is a pointed Gothic arch or a diagonal rib in a vault.

clue.text: Eat some food in eastern restaurants

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, hidden inside them

explanation.surface: Have a meal of dishes in Asian eateries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restaurants' completes the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dine is to have a meal, especially dinner.

clue.text: Quite determined to find Penny new interests

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the next word are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to help a woman named Penny find new hobbies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a name but gives P; 'new' rearranges INTERESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being persistent means refusing to give up, staying steadfastly resolved.
